reason: A value equal to the default namespace IRI, asserted or read from PROV-N, PROV-JSON, PROV-JSONLD (node and value), PROV-XML and PROV-O, raises with the default-namespace reason and the channel's message. #675, which gives such a value the wrong reason.

For asserted code and the PROV-N, PROV-JSON, PROV-JSONLD and PROV-O readers, a value typed `prov:QUALIFIED_NAME` or `xsd:QName` whose text is undeclared, a full IRI, has no prefix or is empty raises with the exact message for its channel and reason. #587, which makes one check and one message for an unresolved name across the model and the readers. #516, #551, #553 also apply.

PROV-JSON, PROV-XML, PROV-JSONLD and PROV-N text with an unresolved element id `zz:e` or relation id `zz:u` raises the reader's error carrying the unresolved-name sentence. #725, which gives every position one error sentence for an unresolvable name.

Ten PROV-JSON documents, with declared and `http`-prefixed record keys, a blank-node key, a typed and a language-tagged value, bundle keys, formal attributes and a member list, read without raising. #551 and #599, whose rejecting rules sit beside this test (rubric rule 6). `test_json.py::test_reader_rejects` holds the rejecting rows.

With `ex` declared and no prefix named `http`, `document.entity("http://example.org/e1")` has the identifier `ex:e1`. `docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md`, which says a plain-string identifier in code still compacts when no prefix named `http` is in scope.

When a bundle declares `ex` and the document declares `http`, the text `http://example.org/a` resolves to the document's `http` name, as an asserted value, an asserted identifier and a PROV-JSON formal attribute. #599, which says a prefix the document declares wins over compaction in a bundle.

PROV-N text with a `'ex:x'` value, a `"ex:x" %% prov:QUALIFIED_NAME` value, a `"ex:x" %% xsd:QName` value, a `'x'` value under a default, an `xsi:x` value with `xsi` declared and a full IRI with a prefix named `http` is read into the expected `QualifiedName`. #516 and #553, which keep a PROV-N value that resolves by its prefix and reject one that does not.
In PROV-N, a bundle's `'ex:x'` value resolves to the document's `ex`, and its `'b:y'` value resolves to the bundle's own `b`. #516 and #599, whose prefix rules a bundle's value follows.

Narrowed: the rows `declared` and `xsd:QName declared` went, and the rows `declared in the document`, `bare name with a default` and `untyped` stay. `test_value_forms.py::test_qualified_name_literal_is_stored_as_a_qualified_name` took the two rows over through its `[prov:QUALIFIED_NAME]` and `[xsd:QName]` ids. It asserts the same `Literal("ex:x", ...)` on `ex_document().entity` and checks `isinstance(value, QualifiedName)` as well as equality, so it asserts more on the same input. The attribute name (`ex:k` here, `ex:v` there) takes the same branch in `ProvRecord._coerce_attribute_value`, and reaches `resolve_name` and `resolve_pair` only to word a rejection. `ProvRecord.extra_attributes` and `ProvRecord.get_attribute` read the same attribute store. Nothing is lost because the verifier planted five faults and none separated a removed row from its takeover. Narrowing the datatype test in `ProvRecord._auto_literal_conversion` to `PROV_QUALIFIEDNAME` alone fails the takeover's `[xsd:QName]` id, and storing a plain `Identifier` fails both takeover ids. Only a fault keyed on the attribute's local name `k` separates the rows, and it is contrived. The mutation check found no arc only these rows covered and no newly undetected mutant. The three remaining rows keep what the takeover lacks, which is a bundle, a bare name under a default and the untyped string. The rows unpack `extra_attributes` as `((_, value),)`, so they also assert that the record holds one non-formal attribute, and the remaining `declared in the document` row still asserts this on the same `PROV_QUALIFIEDNAME` path. Together they pin that an entity asserting a qualified-name literal that resolves stores the expected name, and that an untyped `Literal("zz:x")` stays a string. The contract is #516, #551, #553 and #599, which reject a qualified-name value that does not resolve and keep one that does. The `untyped` row is now the only user of the helper `_in_the_document`.
